name: samples only from the nucleus
test:
samples = [top_p_sample([3.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0], 0.8) for _ in range(200)]
assert set(samples) == {0, 1}
assert all(isinstance(token_id, int) for token_id in samples)
print('ok')

name: returns original token indexes
single-token nucleus is deterministic
test:
samples = [top_p_sample([10.0, 0.0, 0.0], 0.5) for _ in range(20)]
assert samples == [0] * 20
print('ok')

name: top_p one samples the full distribution
temperature changes the nucleus
test:
cold = [top_p_sample([2.0, 0.0], 0.8, temperature=1.0) for _ in range(20)]
hot = [top_p_sample([2.0, 0.0], 0.8, temperature=2.0) for _ in range(200)]
assert cold == [0] * 20
assert set(hot) == {0, 1}
print('ok')

name: top-k keeps exactly k original token ids, breaking ties by index
test:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(105)
samples = [top_k_sample([0.0, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0], 2) for _ in range(200)]
assert set(samples) == {1, 2}
assert all(isinstance(token, int) for token in samples)
assert all(sample_token([0.0, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0], top_k=2, top_p=0.4) == 1 for _ in range(20))
print('ok')

name: top-k samples proportionally instead of uniformly or greedily
test:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(106)
logits = np.log([0.5, 0.3, 0.2])
samples = [top_k_sample(logits, 2) for _ in range(6000)]
assert set(samples) == {0, 1}
assert abs(samples.count(0) / len(samples) - 0.625) < 0.04
print('ok')

name: combined top-p uses the renormalized top-k distribution
input: logits = log([0.5, 0.3, 0.2]), top_k = 2, top_p = 0.6; only token 0 survives
test:
import numpy as np
logits = np.log([0.5, 0.3, 0.2])
samples = [sample_token(logits, top_k=2, top_p=0.6) for _ in range(100)]
assert samples == [0] * 100
print('ok')

name: combined sampling preserves original ids and conditional probabilities
input: logits = log([0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.4]), top_k = 3, top_p = 0.7; IDs 3 and 1 survive with probabilities 4/7 and 3/7
test:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(107)
logits = np.log([0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.4])
samples = [sample_token(logits, top_k=3, top_p=0.7) for _ in range(6000)]
assert set(samples) == {1, 3}
assert all(isinstance(token, int) for token in samples)
assert abs(samples.count(3) / len(samples) - 4/7) < 0.04
print('ok')

name: temperature is applied before the combined nucleus threshold
input: logits = [2, 0, -4], top_k=2, top_p=0.8; T=1 keeps only 0, T=2 allows 0 and 1
test:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(109)
assert all(sample_token([2.0, 0.0, -4.0], top_k=2, top_p=0.8, temperature=1.0) == 0 for _ in range(20))
hot = [sample_token([2.0, 0.0, -4.0], top_k=2, top_p=0.8, temperature=2.0) for _ in range(400)]
assert set(hot) == {0, 1}
print('ok')

name: top-p includes the threshold-crossing token and respects an exact boundary
input: probabilities [0.5, 0.25, 0.25]: p=0.5 keeps ID 0; p=0.6 adds ID 1
test:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(110)
logits = np.log([0.5, 0.25, 0.25])
assert all(top_p_sample(logits, 0.5) == 0 for _ in range(20))
assert set(top_p_sample(logits, 0.6) for _ in range(200)) == {0, 1}
assert set(sample_token(logits, top_k=3, top_p=0.6) for _ in range(200)) == {0, 1}
print('ok')

name: large common offsets, strided arrays, and lists do not mutate inputs
input: large logits on noncontiguous NumPy view and Python list; lower original-index ties
test:
import numpy as np
storage = np.array([10003.0, -999.0, 10000.0, -998.0, 9999.0, -997.0])
logits = storage[::2]
before = storage.copy()
values = [10003.0, 10000.0, 9999.0]
original = values[:]
for _ in range(20):
    assert sample_token(logits, top_k=2, top_p=0.6) == 0
    assert top_k_sample(values, 1) == 0
    assert top_p_sample(values, 0.6) == 0
assert np.array_equal(storage, before)
assert values == original
print('ok')

name: finite extreme logits and temperatures preserve the distribution
input: logits [1e308, -1e308] with temperature=1e308; tied huge logits with a tiny temperature
test:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(111)
samples = [sample_token([1e308, -1e308], temperature=1e308) for _ in range(6000)]
expected = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-2.0))
assert set(samples) == {0, 1}
assert abs(samples.count(0) / len(samples) - expected) < 0.04
assert set(sample_token([1e308, 1e308, -1e308], top_p=0.9, temperature=1e-300) for _ in range(200)) == {0, 1}
print('ok')

name: top-p-only sampling follows conditional probabilities
input: logits = log([0.5, 0.3, 0.2]), top_p=0.7; IDs 0 and 1 have conditional probabilities 0.625 and 0.375
test:

logits = np.log([0.5, 0.3, 0.2])
